brief.text: St. Louis reached a 36-month high median sale price of $305,000 in May 2026, up 7% year-over-year in a seller's market. Monthly payments surged 15% annually, while inventory grew 3.9% and days on market increased slightly to 21. Rent rose 3.7% to $1,425, and the market remains hot relative to the 50 largest metros.

key_points: Median sale price at 36-month high, +3.2% YoY
Rent growth of 5.8% outpacing home values
Monthly payment +11% YoY in seller's market
brief.text: Virginia Beach reached a 36-month high median sale price of $383,340 in May 2026, up 3.2% year-over-year in a seller's market. Inventory fell 8.6% to 5,192 homes while rent growth accelerated to 5.8%, outpacing home value appreciation. Monthly payments surged 11% annually, though median days on market edged up just 2 days to 28.

key_points: Median sale price at 36-month high of $341,000
Strong seller's market with homes selling above list
brief.text: Warren, MI's median sale price hit a 36-month high of $341,000 in May 2026, up 3.3% annually. Monthly payments surged 11% year-over-year, while inventory rose 4.9% to 5,949 units. The market remains a strong seller's market with 2.1 months of supply and homes selling above list price at 100.1%. Relative to the 50 largest metros, this market is hot.

key_points: Median sale price at 36-month high of $630,000
Seller's market with 2.6 months of supply
brief.text: Washington, DC's median sale price hit a 36-month high of $630,000 in May 2026, up 3.5% year-over-year, while monthly payments rose 12% annually. The seller's market remains tight with 2.6 months of supply and inventory up just 0.7%. Days on market increased 2 days to 34, and price drops fell 1.1pp to 26.1% of listings.

key_points: Days on market fell 5 days to 81
brief.text: West Palm Beach's housing inventory fell 12.4% year-over-year to 12,331 homes through May 2026, while median sale prices rose 1.9% to $540,000. Homes sold faster, with days on market dropping 5 days to 81. The market remains balanced with 5.3 months of supply, down 1.1 months annually, and fewer price drops at 24.0% of sales, down 5.2 pp.
